body.text: Start time (date -u): 2026-11-03T03:22:26Z. Eight-hour operator budget; Stage 1 reconstruction deadline 2026-11-03T04:22:26Z. Read task, scene/object specifications, hardware specification, and demo2sim documents. Task: sequentially pick white then black charger from table right, lift and reorient blades-up, move left, release upright. Reconstruction precedes building the training simulation. All results are my own simulation claims.

Reconstruction analysis: white-first then black; supporting table; right hand only. SAM3 masks and known-geometry PyTorch3D pose fitting, HaWoR initialization plus required MANO fitting. Unseeded white fitting reversed blade direction at high IoU; local tracker copy now accepts a PnP initialization. Focal profile is weak (rounded corners and dimension uncertainty); chose 1060 px consistent with MoGe priors 1074/1045 px. Estimated camera motion from background rotation and the passive charger. Rest support is constrained, and hidden/lost object frames stay invalid. Task decomposition is saved in research/TASK_UNDERSTANDING.md.

Re-read updated README stopping rule after operator update. Hard deadline 2026-11-03T11:22Z. Reserve final minutes for a best-policy verification and reflection if no pass occurs earlier. The default MANO fit gave hand-mask IoU 0.829 but only 0.418 contact coverage, indicating a monocular depth mismatch; testing documented fitting settings with larger contact capture radius, fixed scale, and stronger contact/penetration/depth-order terms. No training simulation has been built.

Independent reference checks exposed two errors hidden by the fitter summary: thumb contact was absent (closest middle/ring probes satisfied the loss), and distal fingers intersected in about 30% of valid frames. Support enforcement by vertical shifts also damaged image agreement. Corrected support along camera rays, preserving image centers (frame-0 IoU now 0.838 white/0.892 black). Testing a documented local copy of the required MANO fitter with explicit opposed thumb/finger surface contact and distal-finger separation penalties. The installed tools remain unchanged; these checks are not waived.

Planned learning approach (not yet building the training simulation): a reconstruction-derived wrist/finger reference plus a closed-loop neural residual trained by PPO. This is explicitly permitted by LEARNING.md; scripted replay is a baseline only. The policy will observe noisy encoders, wrist state, object pose estimates and phase, and supply action corrections through the specified impedance/PD controllers. Objects remain passive contact-driven rigid bodies. I will compare a zero-residual ablation and keep task, wrist and hardware metrics separate. Primary methods: https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.06347 (PPO), https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.03201 (residual RL), https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.08050 (residual RL from demonstrations). MuJoCo model semantics: https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/latest/XMLreference.html .

body.summary: Sequential white/black plug transfer reconstructed with common metric support, visible blade direction, HaWoR/MANO hand fitting and explicit opposed-contact/self-collision/table constraints. All ten independent checks pass; format VALID.

reprojection.note: against your own masks: agreement with them is necessary, not sufficient (3D errors along the viewing ray are invisible here)

anatomical_contact.note: a grasp needs the thumb and an opposing finger on opposite sides of the object; single-finger pushes or palm support are legitimate but must be stated in the analysis. Low penetration does not imply contact.

penetration_hand_object.note: unsigned (lower bound) distances where the object mesh is not watertight

self_penetration.note: triangle intersections between different fingers (FCL); counts are not volumes

physics.note: free-flight intervals are given with --flight OBJ=a:b; rest intervals default to object intervals without contact

handedness_scale.note: left/right are the demonstrator's anatomical hands; a hand is never mirrored

camera_focal.note: MoGe intrinsics are a learned prior; the focal should be calibrated against known geometry (camera_calib.py pnp). A large disagreement needs its explanation in NOTES.md (which one is wrong, and why).

body.text: Reconstruction v1 recorded as r0006 at 03:50:37Z, within the 60-minute Stage 1 limit. check_reference VALID; all ten quality checks pass. Native replay median IoU: white 0.815, black 0.820. Opposed-grasp fractions: white 0.848, black 0.968. Maximum full-mesh hand/object penetration 0.61/0.50 mm, no distal finger intersections. Visual comparison still shows weakly constrained white intermediate orientation under partial occlusion; those poses retain large uncertainty. Criteria v1 now recorded before any robot policy evaluation. Begin training-simulation construction next.

First zero-residual dynamic baseline failed: white was pushed about 22 mm in +Y during closing and was not lifted; it remained sideways. The diagnostic terminated on a middle MCP speed violation (8.279 rad/s vs 8.203) during the fast white-to-black transition at 11.918 s. Controllers pass isolated response tests, so change the retargeted closure timing and slow the transition; retain contact-rich RL to correct slip and grasp errors. This was an unlearned analysis baseline, not a reported RL policy or successful verification.

body.reason: Before any RL training/evaluation: explicitly require continuous hand support through transport (no toss shortcut), and specify numerical contact/time conventions and the placement event endpoint. No task or wrist tolerance is relaxed.

simulator.name: MuJoCo
simulator.contacts: elliptic friction cone; condim4 including torsional friction; object/table solref 0.004 1; hand solref 0.006 1; solimp 0.95 0.99 0.001; rigid collision shapes with compliant contacts

scene.robot: Supplied Wuji Hand 2.2 right URDF, exact masses/inertias/axes/limits and vendor STL convex collision hulls; 20 motors with effort saturation and specified armatures.
scene.self_collision: Enabled except the five palm-to-proximal-abduction MCP/CMC housing pairs: convex hulls overlap inside the assembled mechanisms (measured 1.6 mm at neutral for ring/pinky). All inter-finger and other hand collisions remain enabled.
scene.objects: Two passive free bodies: prescribed sharp box bodies and Type-A blade boxes; Blender visuals from reconstruction; exact mass 0.075/0.055 kg, COM 2 mm bladeward, uniform-box inertia estimate. No welds, object forces or object state assignment after reset.
scene.table: 1.20 x 1.20 x 0.03 m, center XY (0.10,0), top z0; floor z-0.75; gravity (0,0,-9.81).
scene.attachment_note: Hardware/object asset checksums identify the supplied public model files; source_manifest.json preserves the scene builder and controller/environment source. Binary archives are not accepted by the record endpoint.

reference.retargeting: Robot -Z follows human wrist-to-MCP centroid, +Y right palm normal, +X completes right-handed basis; 358 supported human wrist frames. Offline collision-aware three-contact IK for thumb/index/middle with continuous joint branches. Contacts across the body Y sides; unequal index/middle axial locations drive in-hand reorientation.
reference.usage: Recorded contact phase ordering, wrist orientations and scene alignment guide a frozen base/reference plus RL residual. Object center lift to z0.065 m; final centers from reconstructed placement. Goal yaw preserves initial blade-gap axis because blade-up is task-critical and hidden yaw is uncertain. Reference time is stretched by 1.3, ending at 32.5 s.
reference.replay: replay.mp4 explicitly shows a kinematic retargeting next to time-scaled human video; it is not a learned or dynamic success rollout.

controllers.wrist: Free 6-DoF root, no workspace constraint. 1 kHz impedance: Kp 2000 N/m, Kd60; rotation20 Nm/rad and0.4; exact hand gravity/COM compensation only; force norm<=30N, torque<=2Nm. Executed targets/linear feedforward <=1m/s and angular <=3rad/s at500Hz. Generalized wrench verified equal to mj_applyFT at root origin (error0).
controllers.fingers: Specified joint PD at1kHz with exact gains, q_target clipping, effort saturation, vendor armatures, and no position/velocity state clipping. Position, speed, torque and finite-action validity checked every1ms; violating episodes terminate.
controllers.encoders: Independent sigma0.002rad and0.05rad/s at500Hz; no contact/force/tactile measurements given to policy.
controllers.policy_interface: Neural network at50Hz, decoded/filter40ms into500Hz target packets held two1ms controller ticks. 14 residual actions: wrist translation3 (0.03m), rotation3 (0.22rad), eight finger synergies. Simulator/controller can accept arbitrary wrist targets; bounded residuals are a policy choice.

body.observations: 100D: noisy 20 q/qd, wrist/reference errors and velocity, perfect simulated object pose/velocity and target-position errors, phase, previous action. Perfect object state substitutes for vision and is a limitation.

initial_conditions.reason: Reconstructed initial side-lying charger poses and early visible wrist approach; wrist raised30mm and moved back20mm to accommodate robot geometry. Objects settle physically for0.2s.
initial_conditions.curriculum: Early white grasp/lift resets hand to a collision-aware open retargeted pose at reference clock2.6s; object state assigned only at reset, then passive. Later full episodes start from the recorded initial scene.

episode.termination: Hardware/action error, fall z<-0.05 or large active-object deviation; timeout. Final standing hold included.

validation.joint_limits_and_actuators: Compared against hardware/hardware_spec.json and RIGHT_HAND.md; armature, effort, range and joint order preserved.
validation.zero_residual_diagnostic: Baseline v2 completes black transfer upright at y0.204 m but loses white, ending sideways at y0.108 m. No hardware violations over36s. This is a failure of the unlearned reference, not a policy pass. RL must learn white grasp/lift/transport corrections.

limitations: Friction, restitution, contact compliance and inertia are inferred; no torque-speed envelope or tactile feedback is available.
Object pose observations are exact simulated state.
Kinematic pressure targets can request1mm pad penetration; actual contacts are resolved dynamically.
A demonstrated-looking base alone does not reliably perform the white manipulation; no RL policy has yet been evaluated.

body.reflection: PPO iteration 1 learned the white opposing grasp, >=15 mm lift and >=20 cm left transfer in all20 evaluation episodes, where the zero-residual baseline failed the lift. Full success is0/20: white is released sideways, and corrections learned only on the white lift interfere with black placement. All20 hardware/integrity checks pass. Mean wrist orientation RMS is about10.6deg white/15.7deg black; position RMS0.0857m/0.0814m exceeds the recorded0.08m bound. Do not relax criteria. Next: train the entire white manipulation with phase-gated lift/contact rewards, stronger blade-axis and released-standing rewards, and a direct human-wrist-position reward. The frozen white base still underdrives rotation; revise its offline retargeting to share a modest, explicitly measured extra wrist rotation with finger rolling, while retaining the same wrist thresholds. Then train the whole two-object sequence and expand randomization.

body.reflection: Iteration2 (1.505M PPO transitions on the full white sequence) still has0/20 full successes. All20 acquire an opposing white grasp and lift, but none maintain held carry or complete placement; the best nominal blade-up error is about62.8deg before slipping. No black grasp succeeds, and the untrained later phase produces middle-PIP speed violations. Planned-clock wrist diagnostics improve to mean position RMS0.0769m white/0.0774m black and white orientation RMS39.2deg; without completed release these are diagnostics, not a passing wrist criterion. The changed offline finger path and partial wrist turn can still abandon a real grasp. Next: anchor the finger reference to the physically achieved grasp, train reorientation from a validated passive held-grasp reset, and give the network independent residual control of all20 finger joints. Keep the original20-episode task/wrist/hardware criteria. Force-allocation analysis produced partial in-hand rotation but its weaker-posture variant dropped the object; it is not a solution or a reported policy.

body.text: Simulation3 accepted as r0021 at05:32:03Z before PPOiteration3 started. Curriculum resets use an actually achieved, independently checked passive pinch (1s drift<=1.06mm over tested torque scales), not an object weld. New initial-state verification guard accepts full nominal scene and rejects heldseed. Training/evaluation decoder equivalence is exact for100 stochastic neural steps. Expanded132obs/26actions RL initialization preserves parent mean outputs within7.45e-9; new optimizer and independent finger exploration. Final policy remains closed-loop RL; no online trajectory optimizer is used.

The original approach/lift RL actor already succeeds locally; isolated rotation training can damage actions on phases it never visits. Proposed architecture: a phase-gated mixture of closed-loop PPO-trained neural actors for acquisition, white reorientation/placement, and black manipulation. Each command residual still comes from an RL-trained network, while the same reconstruction-derived reference and exact hardware PD execute it. This is a hierarchical residual-RL architecture, not a scripted final policy or online optimizer. A full original-state20episode evaluation will judge the composed policy; curriculum progress alone cannot pass.

reward_terms.name: fingertip_proximity
reward_terms.formula: exp(-mean positive thumb/index/middle gap/0.020), only grasp-to-release phase

reward_terms.name: opposed_grasp
reward_terms.formula: thumb and opposing body finger force>=0.05N, angle>=60deg; only contact phase

reward_terms.name: released_stand
reward_terms.formula: after release: left, <=15deg blade-up, bottom within2mm, table support>=0.1N, no hand contact, slow linear/angular motion

reward_terms.name: both_standing
reward_terms.formula: both released-standing conditions after black release

reward_terms.name: wrist_reference
reward_terms.formula: exp(-native wrist position error^2/0.06^2 - native orientation error^2/0.5^2) in manipulation, base reference elsewhere

reward_terms.name: unsupported_carry
reward_terms.formula: -1 if acquired grasp and bottom>5mm but body-contact sum<0.05N for>0.05s
